en: Paṭisambhidāmagga 3 Paññāvagga 3.2.
Discourse on Supernormal Power (Iddhikathā)
What is success (iddhi)? How many kinds of success are there?
How many planes, how many bases, how many steps, and how many roots does success have?
What is success (iddhi)?
Success is so called in the sense of succeeding.
How many kinds of success are there?
The ten kinds of supernormal power (iddhi).
How many planes (bhūmi) are there for supernormal power?
There are four planes for supernormal power, four bases (pāda), eight steps (pada), and sixteen roots (mūla).
What are the ten kinds of supernormal power (*iddhi*)?

Supernormal power through resolve, supernormal power through transformation, supernormal power consisting of mind-made [body], supernormal power through the expansion of knowledge, supernormal power through the expansion of concentration,
noble supernormal power, supernormal power born of the ripening of kamma, supernormal power of one possessing merit, supernormal power consisting of science, and therein—
In this context, success (*iddhi*) is so called in the sense of accomplishment through the condition of right application.
What are the four planes of success?

The first jhāna is the plane born of seclusion; the second jhāna is the plane of rapture and pleasure; the third jhāna is the plane of equanimity and pleasure; the fourth jhāna is the plane of neither-pain-nor-pleasure.

"These four bases of psychic power lead to the attainment of psychic power, the acquisition of psychic power, the transformation of psychic power, the manifestation of psychic power, mastery over psychic power, and fearlessness regarding psychic power.
What are the four feet of psychic power?

Here, a bhikkhu develops the basis of psychic power endowed with concentration due to desire and volitional formations of striving; he develops the basis of psychic power endowed with concentration due to mind and volitional formations of striving..."
He develops the basis for psychic power; he develops the basis for psychic power endowed with the concentration of energy and the volitional formations of striving;
he develops the basis for psychic power endowed with the concentration of investigation and the volitional formations of striving.

These four bases for psychic power lead to the attainment of psychic power, the acquisition of psychic power, the transformation of psychic power, the expansion of psychic power, mastery over psychic power, and fearlessness regarding psychic power.
What are the eight bases for psychic power (iddhi-pāda)?
If a bhikkhu, relying on desire, attains concentration, attains one-pointedness of mind—
desire is not concentration, concentration is not desire.
Desire is one thing, concentration is another.
If a bhikkhu, relying on energy, attains concentration, he attains one-pointedness of mind.
Energy is not concentration; concentration is not energy.
Energy is one thing, concentration is another.
If a bhikkhu, relying on the mind, attains concentration, he attains one-pointedness of mind.
The mind is not concentration; concentration is not the mind.
The mind is one thing, concentration is another.
If a bhikkhu, relying on investigation, attains concentration, he attains one-pointedness of mind.
Investigation is not concentration; concentration is not investigation.
Insight is one thing, concentration is another.

These eight factors of psychic power lead to the attainment of psychic power, the acquisition of psychic power, the transformation of psychic power, the manifestation of psychic power, mastery over psychic power, and fearlessness regarding psychic power.
What are the sixteen roots of psychic power?
A mind that is not uplifted does not waver in sloth; thus it is "imperturbable" (āneñja).
A mind that is not elated does not waver in agitation; thus it is "imperturbable.
A mind that is not drawn forward does not waver in lust; thus it is "imperturbable."
The mind that is through mindfulness of breathing does not waver in ill will; thus it is imperturbable.
The mind that is independent does not waver in views; thus it is imperturbable.
The mind that is unbound does not waver in desire and lust; thus it is imperturbable.
A mind that is completely liberated does not waver in sensual lust; thus it is "imperturbable" (āneñja).
A mind that is dissociated does not waver in defilements; thus it is "imperturbable.
A mind for which the barriers have been broken down does not waver at the barrier of defilements; thus it is "imperturbable."
The mind that has attained unity does not waver due to the various defilements; thus it is imperturbable (āneñja).
The mind embraced by faith does not waver in lack of faith; thus it is imperturbable.
The mind embraced by energy does not waver in indolence; thus it is imperturbable.
A mind embraced by mindfulness does not waver in negligence; thus it is imperturbable.
A mind embraced by concentration does not waver in agitation; thus it is imperturbable.
A mind embraced by wisdom does not waver in ignorance; thus it is imperturbable.
A mind that has reached illumination does not waver in the darkness of ignorance; thus it is "imperturbable" (*āneñja*).

These sixteen roots of psychic power lead to the attainment of psychic power, the acquisition of psychic power, the transformation of psychic power, the radiance of psychic power, mastery over psychic power, and fearlessness regarding psychic power.
3.2.1. Exposition of the Ten Psychic Powers (*Dasiddhiniddesa*)
What is success through resolution?
Here, a bhikkhu wields the various kinds of psychic power:
having been one, he becomes many; having been many, he becomes one.
He appears and disappears;
he passes unhindered through walls, through enclosures, and through mountains, as if through space;
and he dives in and out of the earth, as if in water.
He walks on water without breaking the surface, just as on earth;
he travels through the air cross-legged, just like a winged bird;
and he touches and strokes with his hand these very sun and moon, so powerful and majestic.
"Even as far as the Brahma-world, he wields mastery with his body.

Herein, "here" means in this view, in this approval, in this preference, in this adoption, in this Dhamma, in this Vinaya, in this Dhamma-Vinaya, in this teaching, in this holy life, in this Teacher’s dispensation.
Therefore it is said:
“Here”: a monk who is either a virtuous worldling (*puthujjanakalyāṇaka*), a trainee (*sekha*), or an arahant whose nature is unshakable.
“He experiences various kinds of psychic power (*iddhividha*)” means he experiences psychic power in its many different modes.
“Having been one, he becomes many”: being naturally one, he adverts to being many—he adverts to being a hundred, or a thousand, or a hundred thousand.
Having so adverted, he resolves with knowledge:
“Let me be many.”
He becomes many.
Just as the Venerable Cūḷapanthaka, having been one, became many, even so that possessor of psychic power who has attained mastery over his mind, having been one, becomes many.
And having been many, he becomes one again: normally being many, he adverts to being one.
Having adverted [to this], he resolves with knowledge:
"May I be one.
He becomes one.
Just as the venerable Cūḷapanthaka, having become many, becomes one again; even so does that possessor of psychic power, attained to mastery over the mind, having become many, become one again.
"Manifestation" means it becomes uncovered by anything, unobstructed, open, and evident.
"Invisibility" means it becomes covered by something, obstructed, closed, and concealed.
He goes unhindered through walls, through enclosures, and through mountains, as if through open space; for he is naturally one who has attained mastery over the space-kasina.
He adverts to the wall, the enclosure, and the mountain.
Having adverted to them, he resolves upon them with knowledge:
"Let there be space.
There is space.
He goes unhindered through walls, through enclosures, and through mountains.
Just as people who are by nature without psychic power walk unhindered through anything that is not covered or enclosed,
even so does that possessor of psychic power, attained to mastery over his mind, pass unhindered through walls, through enclosures, and through mountains,
as if through open space.
He performs acts of diving in and out of the earth as if it were water; thus he is naturally a master of the attainment of the water-kasiṇa.
He adverts to the earth.
Having adverted to it, he resolves upon it with knowledge:
"Let there be water. There was water.
He performed the act of diving in and out of the earth.

Just as people who naturally lack supernormal power emerge from and submerge in water, even so that possessor of supernormal power, having attained mastery over his mind, emerges from and submerges in earth as if in water.
He walks on water without breaking the surface, as if on earth; for he is one who naturally possesses the attainment of the earth-kasiṇa.
He adverts to the water.
Having adverted with knowledge, he resolves:
"Let there be earth.
It becomes earth.
Thus he walks upon unbroken water.

Just as ordinary people, lacking supernormal power, walk upon solid ground, even so that possessor of supernormal power, having attained mastery over the mind, walks upon unbroken water as if on solid ground.
He also travels through the air cross-legged, like a winged bird; for he is naturally one who has attained the meditative absorption of the earth-kasiṇa.
He adverts to space.
Having adverted to it, he resolves with knowledge:
"Let there be earth."
There is earth.
He walks, stands, sits, and lies down in the air, in the sky.
Just as ordinary people, who naturally lack supernormal power, walk, stand, sit, and lie down upon the earth;

Just as a skilled weaver or his apprentice might spread out a cloth, even so that possessor of psychic power, attained to mastery over the mind, walks, stands, sits, and lies down in the open space of the sky, just like a winged bird.

And these very sun and moon, so powerful and majestic, he touches and strokes with his hand; here, that possessor of psychic power, attained to mastery over the mind, while sitting or lying down, directs his attention toward the sun and moon.
Having adverted with knowledge, he resolves:
"Let it be within arm's reach.
It becomes within arm's reach.
Whether sitting or lying down, he touches, strokes, and rubs the moon and sun with his hand.
Just as ordinary people who lack supernormal power might touch, stroke, and rub some physical object within the reach of their hands,
even so does that possessor of supernormal power, attained to mastery over mind, while sitting or lying down, [touch] the moon and sun.
He touches, strokes, and rubs with his hand.

"He wields power with his body even as far as the Brahma-world" means that if that possessor of psychic power, having attained mastery over the mind, desires to go to the Brahma-world, he resolves upon the distant as being near, thinking:
"Let it be near."
It is near. Even when it is near, one resolves upon it as being far, thinking:
"Let it be far."
It becomes distant.
Even what is much he resolves to be little,
thinking, "Let it be little."
It is small. He resolves that even what is small shall become much, thinking:
"Let it be much."
It becomes extensive.
With the divine eye, he sees the form of that Brahmā;
with the divine ear-element, he hears the voice of that Brahmā.
By means of the knowledge of penetrating the minds of others, he understands the mind of that Brahmā.

If that possessor of psychic power who has attained mastery over the mind wishes to go to the Brahma-world with his visible body, he directs his mind according to the body and resolves his mind according to the body.

Having directed his mind according to the body and resolved his mind according to the body, and having entered upon the perception of pleasure and the perception of lightness, he goes to the Brahma-world with his visible body.

If that possessor of psychic power who has attained mastery over the mind wishes to go to the Brahma-world with an invisible body, he transforms his body by means of the mind; he resolves upon the body by means of the mind.

Having transformed his body by means of the mind and resolved upon the body by means of the mind, and having entered into the perception of bliss and the perception of lightness, he goes to the Brahma-world with an invisible body.
He manifests before that Brahmā a material form, mind-made, complete in all its limbs and parts, with no faculties lacking.
If that possessor of psychic power walks, the emanation also walks there;
if that possessor of psychic power stands, the emanation also stands there;
if that possessor of psychic power sits, the emanation also sits there.
If that possessor of psychic power prepares a bed, the created being also prepares a bed there.
If that possessor of psychic power emits smoke, the created being also emits smoke there.
If that possessor of psychic power blazes up, the created being also blazes up there.
If that possessor of psychic power speaks the Dhamma, the created being also speaks the Dhamma there.
If that possessor of psychic power asks a question, the created being also asks a question there.
If that possessor of psychic power, being asked a question, provides an answer, the created being also, being asked a question there, provides an answer.

If that possessor of psychic power stands together with that Brahmā, converses with him, and engages in discussion with him, then the created being also stands together with that Brahmā, converses with him, and engages in discussion with him there.
Whatever that possessor of psychic power does, the created being does that very same thing— this is success by resolution.
What is supernormal power as transformation?

The Blessed One Sikhī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, had a disciple named Abhibhū who, while standing in the Brahma-world, made himself heard by his voice throughout a thousandfold world-system.
He taught the Dhamma even with a visible body.
He taught the Dhamma with his body invisible;
he taught the Dhamma with the lower half of his body visible and the upper half invisible;
and he taught the Dhamma with the upper half of his body visible and the lower half invisible.
Thus, having abandoned his natural form, he displays the form of a youth, or displays the form of a nāga,
or displays the form of a supaṇṇa, or displays the form of a yakkha, or displays the form of Indra, or displays the form of a deva,
or displays the form of Brahmā, or displays the form of the ocean, or displays the form of a mountain, or displays the form of a forest.
or he displays the form of a lion, or he displays the form of a tiger, or he displays the form of a leopard, or he displays an elephant,
or he displays a horse, or he displays a chariot, or he displays a foot soldier,
or he displays various military arrays.
This is the supernormal power of transformation.
What is the supernormal power of the mind-made?
Here, a bhikkhu manifests from this body another body, material, mind-made, complete in all its limbs and parts, with no faculty lacking.
Just as if a man were to pull a reed from its sheath, it would occur to him:
"This is the sheath; this is the reed."
"The reed is one thing, the sheath is another;
yet the sheath is drawn out from the very reed.
Or again, it is as if a man were to draw a sword from its scabbard.
It would occur to him:
"This is the sword; this is the scabbard. The sword is one thing, the scabbard is another."
“You were indeed born from a silken cloth.
Or, suppose a man were to pull a snake out of its slough;
it would occur to him thus:
“This is the snake; this is the basket.
The snake is one thing, the basket another.
Yet the snake has been drawn out from the basket.”
In the same way, a bhikkhu emanates from this body another body, possessing form, mind-made, complete in all its limbs and parts, and not lacking any faculties.
This is supernormal power consisting of the mind-made.
What is supernormal power consisting of the expansion of knowledge?
The meaning of abandoning the perception of permanence through the contemplation of impermanence succeeds;
this is success by the expansion of knowledge.
Through the contemplation of suffering, the perception of pleasure...
Through the contemplation of non-self, the perception of self;
through the contemplation of disenchantment, delight;
through the contemplation of dispassion, lust.
Through the contemplation of cessation,
the meaning of abandoning arising succeeds; through the contemplation of relinquishment, the meaning of abandoning grasping succeeds—
this is success by the expansion of knowledge.

The psychic power of the venerable Bākula through the expansion of knowledge; the psychic power of the venerable Saṅkicca through the expansion of knowledge; the psychic power of the venerable Bhūtapāla through the expansion of knowledge.
This is the psychic power of the expansion of knowledge.
What is the psychic power of the expansion of concentration?
By means of the first jhāna, the sense of abandoning the hindrances succeeds;
thus it is success through the intervention of concentration.
By means of the second jhāna, the sense of abandoning applied and sustained thought succeeds...
Supernormal power through the expansion of concentration:
by means of the third jhāna, the sense of the abandoning of rapture succeeds; ... pe ...
by means of the fourth jhāna, the sense of the abandoning of pleasure and pain succeeds; ... pe ...

The sense of abandoning the perception of form, the perception of resistance, and the perception of diversity succeeds through the attainment of the base of infinite space … [and so on] … the sense of abandoning the perception of the base of infinite space succeeds through the attainment of the base of infinite consciousness … [and so on] … the sense of abandoning the perception of the base of infinite consciousness succeeds through the attainment of the base of nothingness … [and so on] …
The meaning of the abandoning of the perception of the base of nothingness through the attainment of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception succeeds;
thus it is success by the expansion of concentration.
It is the success by the expansion of concentration of the Venerable Sāriputta, the success by the expansion of concentration of the Venerable Sañjīva.

Supernormal power: the supernormal power of the venerable Khāṇu-koṇḍañña through the expansion of concentration; the supernormal power of the female lay follower Uttarā through the expansion of concentration;
the supernormal power of the female lay follower Sāmāvatī through the expansion of concentration.
This is supernormal power through the expansion of concentration.
What is noble supernormal power?
Here, a bhikkhu, if he should wish:
"May I dwell perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive," dwells there perceiving the unrepulsive.
If he wishes:
"May I dwell perceiving the repulsive in the non-repulsive," he dwells there perceiving the repulsive.
If he wishes—
“If I were to dwell perceiving the unrepulsive in both the repulsive and the unrepulsive,” he dwells there perceiving the unrepulsive.
If he should wish,
“May I dwell perceiving the repulsive in both the unrepulsive and the repulsive,” he dwells there perceiving the repulsive.
If he wishes:
“May I dwell equanimous, mindful and clearly comprehending, having turned away from both the repulsive and the non-repulsive,” he dwells there equanimous, mindful and clearly comprehending.
How does he dwell perceiving the non-repulsive in the repulsive?
Toward an unattractive object, he either pervades it with loving-kindness or resolves it in terms of the elements.
In this way, he dwells perceiving the non-repulsive in the repulsive.
How does he dwell perceiving the repulsive in the non-repulsive?
Toward a desirable object, one pervades it with the perception of foulness or brings it into connection with impermanence.
In this way, one dwells perceiving the unrepulsive as repulsive.
How does one dwell perceiving both the repulsive and the unrepulsive as unrepulsive?
Toward both an undesirable object and a desirable object, he either pervades it with loving-kindness or resolves it in terms of its elements.
In this way, he dwells perceiving the non-repulsive in both the repulsive and the non-repulsive.
How does he dwell perceiving the repulsive in both the repulsive and the non-repulsive?
Whether toward a desirable object or an undesirable object, one pervades it with the perception of foulness or contemplates it as impermanent.
In this way, one dwells perceiving the repulsive in both the non-repulsive and the repulsive.
How does one dwell equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending, having avoided both the repulsive and the non-repulsive?
Here, bhikkhus, having seen a form with the eye, a bhikkhu is neither glad nor sad; he dwells in equanimity, mindful and clearly comprehending.
Having heard a sound with the ear...
[and so on] ...having smelled an odor with the nose...
Having tasted a flavor with the tongue...
having touched a tangible object with the body...
having cognized a mental phenomenon with the mind, one is neither glad nor sad; one dwells in equanimity, mindful and clearly comprehending.
Thus, having avoided both the repulsive and the non-repulsive, he dwells in equanimity, mindful and clearly comprehending.
This is noble psychic power (*ariyā iddhi*).
What is psychic power born of the maturation of kamma (*kammavipākajā iddhi*)?
For all birds, for all devas, for some humans, and for some beings in the states of deprivation—
this is success born of the ripening of kamma.
What is the success of one possessing merit?
A wheel-turning monarch travels through the air together with his fourfold army, including even the horse-grooms and stable-boys.
Such is the psychic power of the merit of the householder Jotika; such is the psychic power of the merit of the householder Jaṭila; such is the psychic power of the merit of the householder Meṇḍaka;
such is the psychic power of the merit of the householder Ghosita; such is the psychic power of the merit of the five great meritorious ones.
This is the psychic power of one possessed of merit.
What is the psychic power consisting of knowledge?

Those who possess the spells, having recited the spell, travel through the air; they display an elephant in the sky, in the atmosphere, they display a horse, they display a chariot, they display a foot soldier, and they display various military arrays.
This is supernormal power consisting of science (*vijjāmayā iddhi*).
How, in this context, is it "success" (*iddhi*) in the sense of succeeding through the condition of right application here and there?
It is because the abandoning of sensual desire succeeds by means of renunciation.
In each respective case, it is success (*iddhi*) in the sense of accomplishment through the condition of right application.
Because the abandoning of ill will through non-ill will succeeds, it is success in the sense of accomplishment through the condition of right application in each respective case ... [and so on] ...
The meaning of the abandoning of all defilements through the path of arahantship succeeds;
thus, in each respective case, it is success (*iddhi*) in the sense of succeeding by way of the condition of right application.
In this way, it is success in the sense of succeeding by way of the condition of right application in each respective case.
These are the ten supernormal powers.
The discussion on supernormal powers is finished.
